The guards were sure your trunk was main

Two PreToolUse guards carried a literal branch name. Pick the repo your stack actually lives in and watch what each one used to say.

worktree-merge-verifier: which branch it measures against

resolveBase()
  before  
  after

delete-branch-stacked-pr-guard: the recovery line it prints

before  git rebase origin/main
        gh pr edit <N> --base main

after

The trunk name was only half the bug. A squash merge puts the parent on the trunk as one new commit, so a plain rebase replays the parent's original commits and conflicts on every one of them. The --onto form drops them instead, which is why the recorded parent tip is part of the advice rather than a footnote.

The test that failed first

AssertionError: expected 'origin/main' to be 'origin/develop'
  Tests  6 failed | 5 passed (11)      before
  Tests  11 passed (11)                after

The suite builds real throwaway repos with both origin/main and origin/develop present and origin/HEAD pointing at develop, so a guard that guesses a familiar name cannot pass by luck. The delete-branch cases drive the hook end to end through a stub gh on PATH and assert the printed string, not an internal helper.

One new lib module (lib/git-trunk.ts), no new hook, no registration change. Fallback names are tried only when origin/HEAD is unset, and the guard says so out loud rather than inventing a trunk.
